task: Implement POST /api/contact in api_server.py (Contact Us form-to-email via Resend)
what_went_wrong: First implementation raised UnboundLocalError on _contact_hits inside the handler (module-level dict read + reassigned without 'global' declaration) -> HTTP 500 on every valid payload. A secondary process issue compounded it: two stale api_server processes (pids 2356, 7164, both started 17:17:13) held port 8000, with the listener running pre-fix code, so the post-fix re-test still returned 500 and the traceback displayed line content from the edited file while executing the old compiled frame - misleading diagnosis.
root_cause: 1) Missing 'global' declaration for module-level mutable state mutated in a handler; written without scope check. 2) Local test harness did not verify which process was listening on the test port, so tests ran against a stale instance.
what_i_actually_did_wrong: Shipped the handler without reviewing scope rules for the rate-limit dict, then trusted a re-test that never validated the listener identity - wasted a diagnostic cycle on a phantom 'fix didn't apply' theory.
fix: Added 'global _contact_hits' (api_server.py:354); killed pids 2356/7164; confirmed port free; restarted one clean venv instance; re-tested: 503 not-configured and 429 rate-limit both as specified.
lesson: Before any endpoint test: assert exactly one listener on the port and confirm its start time post-dates the last code edit. Review scope declarations on first write of module-level mutable state.
